title: Lemon balm glycerite for anxiety in children
subtitle: An alcohol-free lemon balm preparation for anxious or restless school-age children
excerpt: Dried lemon balm leaf macerated in vegetable glycerine for four to six weeks to produce a sweet, alcohol-free preparation for anxiety and sleep support in school-age children (6 to 12 years). A glycerite uses vegetable glycerine instead of alcohol as the menstruum. One ml per dose for children, up to twice daily. Not suitable for children under six years old.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931) : Melissa officinalis, nervine and sedative properties. EMA HMPC monograph on Melissa officinalis (2013) : traditional-use assessment including mild sedative action. Woelk et al. (2006), Phytomedicine : lemon balm and valerian for sleep in children (combination study). Glycerite preparation method synthesised from modern western herbal practice: glycerine as a paediatric-safe menstruum replacing alcohol in children's preparations. Thyroid caution at high dose noted in EMA assessment. Paediatric dosing follows standard practice of 1 ml per dose for children 6 to 12 years, per herbalist consensus in modern UK practice.

recipe.yieldDescription: About 100 ml glycerite (approximately 50 child doses at 1 ml each)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Maceration takes 4 to 6 weeks. The finished glycerite keeps 12 months in dark glass.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Store in amber glass in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps 12 months from the strain date. Glycerites have a shorter shelf life than alcohol tinctures.

glossaryTerms.definition: An alcohol-free herbal preparation that uses vegetable glycerine as the menstruum (the liquid used for extraction) instead of alcohol. Glycerine is sweet, mild, and safe for children. It extracts water-soluble plant constituents but is less efficient at oil-soluble ones compared with alcohol tinctures.
The liquid used to extract constituents from plant material in a herbal preparation. Water is the menstruum in an infusion; alcohol in a tincture; glycerine in a glycerite.

projectSchedule.title: Start your glycerite
projectSchedule.body: Pack the dried lemon balm leaf into a clean maceration jar. Pour over the vegetable glycerine until the herb is fully submerged with at least 2 cm above. The glycerine is thick; stir with a clean spoon to work out air bubbles. Seal the jar tightly and label with the herb name, the menstruum (glycerine), and today's date. Store in a cool dark cupboard.

projectSchedule.title: Check and stir
projectSchedule.body: The glycerine should have softened the herb. Stir gently and check the herb is still fully submerged. Glycerine is dense and moves slowly; a quick stir helps it contact all the plant material. Seal and return to the cupboard.

projectSchedule.title: Taste and check
projectSchedule.body: Taste a few drops on a clean spoon. The glycerite should be sweet with a clear lemon note from the lemon balm. No bitterness or off-smell. If it tastes good and smells of lemon balm, it is coming along well. Leave for another two weeks.

projectSchedule.title: Strain and bottle
projectSchedule.body: Your glycerite is ready. Line a sieve with a double layer of muslin over a clean jug. Pour through and press the spent herb firmly. Glycerine is thick, so this takes a little patience. Funnel into amber dropper bottles. Label with the herb, the menstruum (glycerine), the strain date, and the child-dose guidance.

content.text: Lemon balm glycerite is an alcohol-free preparation: dried lemon balm leaf macerated in vegetable glycerine instead of spirit. This makes it a safe and appropriate preparation for school-age children. A

(the extraction liquid): it is sweet, mild, and free of alcohol. It extracts the water-soluble nerve-calming active compounds of lemon balm that are associated with the herb's traditional use for anxiety, restlessness, and sleep. The preparation takes four to six weeks to macerate. The result is a pale, lemon-scented sweet liquid, pleasant for children to take. The dose for children aged 6 to 12 is 1 ml, once or twice daily. Adults can use 2 to 4 ml. Do not use in children under six years old.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms. Age restriction: this preparation is for children aged 6 to 12 years. Do not give to children under 6 years old. For children under six with anxiety or sleep difficulties, consult a paediatric herbalist or your GP. Paediatric dosing is not adult dosing divided by body weight; the age band matters. Thyroid: high doses of lemon balm have been studied for hyperthyroid symptoms; at the doses in this preparation (1 ml for children), this is not a concern, but readers on thyroid hormone replacement should consult their prescriber before use. No significant drug interactions at this preparation strength have been documented at child doses.

items.prepNote: food-grade vegetable glycerine; this is the menstruum, replacing alcohol

content.text: Pack the dried lemon balm into a clean soaking period jar. Pour over the vegetable glycerine. Glycerine is thicker than water or spirit, so stir gently with a clean spoon to work out air pockets and ensure the herb is fully coated and covered. The herb should be submerged with at least 2 cm of glycerine above the top. Seal tightly. Label with the herb name, 'glycerine', and today's date.
Step 2: Macerate four to six weeks

Store in a cool, dark cupboard. Stir or shake every few days; because glycerine is dense, movement helps it contact all parts of the herb. After two weeks, check the herb is still submerged. At four weeks, taste a few drops: it should be distinctly sweet and lemony. Leave for up to six weeks for a fuller extraction.

Line a sieve with a double layer of muslin over a clean jug. Pour through and press the spent herb firmly. Glycerine is slow to drain; allow a few minutes. Funnel into amber glass dropper bottles. Label with the herb, menstruum, strain date, and the dosing guidance for the age band.

Children aged 6 to 12 years: 1 ml per dose, once or twice a day. Give as a single dose in the evening for sleep support, or a morning and evening dose for daytime anxiety. Adults: 2 to 4 ml, once or twice daily. Do not give to children under 6 years old. Course: up to four weeks. If there is no improvement or the anxiety or sleep problems worsen, consult a GP or paediatric herbalist rather than continuing.

Store in amber glass dropper bottles in a cool, dark cupboard. Keeps 12 months from the strain date. Glycerites have a shorter shelf life than alcohol tinctures. Discard if the smell changes or if anything unusual develops in the bottle.
When not to use this remedy

Do not give to children under 6 years old. Do not give to a child on thyroid medication without consulting the prescriber. See a GP for anxiety that interferes with the child's daily life, school attendance, or relationships; for sleep problems lasting more than a few weeks; or for any anxiety with low mood, significant weight changes, or withdrawal. Childhood anxiety with these features needs assessment, not a home remedy alone.
